subject: Data Engineering
title: Who Invented the Data Lake?
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Who Invented the Data Lake?.

hook.text: In 2010, Pentaho CTO James Dixon coined the term 'data lake' as an alternative to the data warehouse.

buildup.text: Dixon argued that warehouses forced you to decide what data was valuable before you could store it.

discovery.text: The lake metaphor meant: capture all the water first. Bottle and filter it when you need to drink.

twist.text: Hadoop made lakes practical by offering cheap distributed storage. Without Hadoop, lakes were just a nice idea.

climax.text: The concept evolved far beyond Dixon's original vision as cloud storage made lakes truly unlimited in scale.

punchline.text: Store first. Decide later. That was the lake's radical idea.
